title: Positive variance forces positive degree
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space. Suppose every component of $f$ indexed by a coordinate subset of size greater than $k$ vanishes identically, and suppose the variance of $f$ under $P$ is positive. Then $k>0$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with positive coordinate weights summing to one
$f$ is real-valued on the product space
Every component indexed by a subset of size greater than $k$ vanishes at every outcome
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$, and $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)>0$. Then $k>0$.
